editorialStandard: Themes describe cultural and economic associations, not NaijaDeals supply availability. Rankings and volume claims appear only where the cited source states them. Trade values are as reported by World Bank WITS (UN Comtrade data) for 2023 unless the source says otherwise. Themes with no adequate fetched source carry reviewStatus needs-source.

countries.name: Angola
countries.introduction: Angola runs from Atlantic fishing towns to the Central Plateau, where cassava, maize and beans underpin household food supply. Coffee, palm oil and diamond exports connect that agricultural base to world markets beyond the oil sector.

themes.label: Coffee
themes.association: Angola's agriculture ministry has set out a diversification strategy covering palm oil, soybeans, coffee and cereals, as reported by FAO's country office. Coffee is one of four crops the ministry names in that agenda.

themes.label: Palm oil
themes.association: Palm oil appears alongside coffee, soybeans and cereals in the agricultural strategy FAO reports for Angola, one of the crops named in the ministry's diversification plan.

themes.label: Cassava
themes.association: A joint FAO/WFP crop assessment described cassava as the main staple in Angola's northern provinces and put 2003/04 output at 6.64 million tonnes, with the north producing 84% of the total. The assessment treats cassava as the country's second food crop by planted area.

sources.title: Missão conjunta FAO/PMA de avaliação das colheitas e do abastecimento alimentar em Angola

themes.label: Maize and beans
themes.association: The same FAO/WFP assessment estimated maize output at 576,917 tonnes in 2003/04 and described maize and beans as the dominant crops of Angola's Central Plateau.

sources.title: Missão conjunta FAO/PMA de avaliação das colheitas e do abastecimento alimentar em Angola

themes.label: Honey
themes.association: FAO's regional review of non-wood forest products describes beekeeping in Angola as mainly a subsistence activity, with potential in the country's nectar-producing plants and eucalyptus plantations.

sources.title: Non-wood forest products in Africa: a regional and national overview

themes.label: Industrial diamonds
themes.association: World Bank WITS lists unworked industrial diamonds as one of Angola's largest exports in 2023 at about US$1.59 billion, behind petroleum oils and liquefied natural gas.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Angola

countries.name: Botswana
countries.introduction: Botswana is a semi-arid country where cattle ranching and diamond mining have shaped the modern economy. Beef, soda ash, copper and vehicle wiring sets lead exports, alongside indigenous crafts sold through curio shops in Gaborone, Francistown, Maun and Kasane.

themes.label: Beef
themes.association: The Botswana Meat Commission, a parastatal founded in 1965, operates abattoirs at Lobatse, Francistown and Maun and lists the UK, Netherlands, Italy, Germany and South Africa among its export markets. FAO's Botswana office has urged Nata-Gweta beef producers to invest in compliance and certification for regional and international markets.

themes.label: Diamonds
themes.association: Debswana, established in 1969, operates the Jwaneng, Orapa, Letlhakane and Damtshaa mines and describes itself as one of the world's foremost diamond producers by value and volume.

themes.label: Indigenous crafts
themes.association: Botswana's tourism board notes that indigenous crafts are sold through curio, craft and gift shops in Gaborone, Francistown, Maun and Kasane and at safari camps, and describes the mokoro canoe, dug from ebony or kigelia trunks, as an Okavango Delta tradition.

themes.label: Soda ash
themes.association: World Bank WITS records disodium carbonate, or soda ash, among Botswana's top five exports in 2023 at about US$56 million, an industrial chemicals line traded alongside diamonds and copper.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Botswana

themes.label: Vehicle wiring sets
themes.association: Ignition and other wiring sets for vehicles were Botswana's fourth-largest export in 2023 at about US$123 million, according to World Bank WITS, evidence of vehicle-component manufacturing.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Botswana

themes.label: Copper ore
themes.association: Copper ores and concentrates ranked third among Botswana's exports in 2023 at about US$507 million, World Bank WITS data show.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Botswana

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.introduction: Eswatini sits between South Africa and Mozambique, with irrigated cane fields in the lowveld and timber plantations in the highveld. Sugar, sawn timber, handcrafted candles and flavouring compounds anchor an export trade that also includes coal and bananas.

themes.label: Sugar
themes.association: The Eswatini Sugar Association states that the industry sells into four markets — the domestic SACU market, the EU, the US and regional markets — and contributes 6.3% of GDP with annual revenue above E7 billion.

themes.label: Handcrafted candles
themes.association: Swazi Candles, established in 1982 in the Malkerns Valley, makes millifiore candles, glycerine soaps and marula oil balm, employs 45 people permanently and exports to more than 20 countries.

themes.label: Timber
themes.association: Montigny Investments describes itself as the largest privately owned integrated timber company in Southern Africa, owning over 55,000 hectares of certified plantation and selling treated timber, biomass, pulp and chipboard.

themes.label: Flavouring compounds
themes.association: Mixtures of odoriferous substances were Eswatini's largest export in 2023 at about US$584 million, according to World Bank WITS — a flavouring and fragrance manufacturing line ahead of raw cane sugar.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Eswatini

themes.label: Coal
themes.association: Other coal ranked fifth among Eswatini's exports in 2023 at about US$72 million, World Bank WITS data show.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Eswatini

themes.label: Bananas
themes.association: FAO's Eswatini office reports training that builds national surveillance capacity against Fusarium wilt of banana, a disease affecting one of the country's established fruit crops.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.introduction: Lesotho is a high-altitude kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, where mountain water, wool and mohair shape rural livelihoods. Garments, bottled water, diamonds and automotive components make up most of its recorded export earnings, according to World Bank trade data.

themes.label: Garments and textiles
themes.association: The Lesotho National Development Corporation states that Lesotho is among Africa's top four producers of textiles and garments, and World Bank WITS lists men's cotton trousers and T-shirts among its five largest exports in 2023. The World Bank describes textiles as the country's largest private employer.

themes.label: Wool
themes.association: Greasy wool was Lesotho's fourth-largest export in 2023 at about US$39 million, according to World Bank WITS, and the national development corporation lists wool and mohair among export opportunities.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Lesotho

themes.label: Mohair
themes.association: The Lesotho National Development Corporation lists mohair, alongside wool, as an export opportunity and presents the sector as part of the country's livestock economy.

themes.label: Highland water
themes.association: Mineral and aerated waters were Lesotho's second-largest export in 2023 at about US$72 million, World Bank WITS shows, consistent with the development corporation's emphasis on plentiful highland water.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Lesotho

themes.label: Trout
themes.association: The Lesotho National Development Corporation lists trout among the country's export opportunities, alongside diamonds, water and apparel.

themes.label: Automotive components
themes.association: Lesotho's development corporation reports a growing position in automotive components, electronics and electrical products, extending the country's manufacturing base beyond garments.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.introduction: Malawi follows the Great Rift Valley from Lake Malawi to the tea and macadamia estates of Thyolo and Mulanje. Tobacco, tea, sugar and groundnuts dominate exports, while agriculture employs over 80% of the population and most households farm maize.

themes.label: Tea
themes.association: Black tea was Malawi's second-largest export in 2023 at about US$70 million, per World Bank WITS, and the Malawi Investment and Trade Centre names tea among the crops its land and climate support.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Malawi

themes.label: Tobacco
themes.association: Tobacco, partly or wholly stemmed, was Malawi's largest export in 2023 at about US$427 million, according to World Bank WITS.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Malawi

themes.label: Sugar
themes.association: Raw cane sugar ranked fifth among Malawi's exports in 2023 at about US$42 million, World Bank WITS data show.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Malawi

themes.label: Groundnuts
themes.association: Shelled groundnuts were Malawi's third-largest export in 2023 at about US$54 million, per World Bank WITS.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Malawi

themes.label: Macadamia
themes.association: The Malawi Investment and Trade Centre names macadamia nuts among the crops that Malawi's fertile land and climate support, alongside tea and coffee.

themes.label: Honey
themes.association: FAO's regional non-wood forest products review estimates about 8,000 Malawian beekeepers producing 1,000 tonnes of honey and 150 tonnes of beeswax a year, while 80% of honey consumed in the country is imported.

sources.title: Non-wood forest products in Africa: a regional and national overview

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.introduction: Mozambique's long Indian Ocean coast and fertile river valleys support cashew, cotton and oilseed farming. Aluminium, coal and natural gas dominate recorded export value, while honey and palm-leaf weaving support rural trade in the interior.

themes.label: Cashew
themes.association: Mozambique's Cashew Institute (IAM) describes its mission as promoting production, marketing, processing and export of cashew, and set a 2024/25 reference price of 45 meticais per kilogram, later raised to 48. FAO's MAFAP programme calls cashew a key Mozambican commodity and a former export leader, and reviewed the price formula at IAM's request in 2023.

sources.title: FAO MAFAP — Review of cashew reference price-setting in Mozambique

themes.label: Cotton
themes.association: The Cotton and Oilseeds Institute of Mozambique (IAOM), created by decree in 2020, regulates cotton and oilseeds and reports cotton output of 23,516 tonnes in the 2022/23 campaign.

sources.title: Instituto do Algodão e Oleaginosas de Moçambique (IAOM)

themes.label: Sesame and oilseeds
themes.association: IAOM's 2022/23 figures put sesame at 191,639 tonnes, far above its 74,120 tonnes of soy and 5,703 tonnes of sunflower, making sesame the institute's largest reported oilseed.

sources.title: Instituto do Algodão e Oleaginosas de Moçambique (IAOM)

themes.label: Honey
themes.association: FAO's regional review estimates 20,000 traditional beekeepers in Mozambique producing 360 tonnes of honey and 60 tonnes of beeswax a year, and notes that smoke-heavy harvesting reduces quality.

sources.title: Non-wood forest products in Africa: a regional and national overview

themes.label: Palm-leaf weaving
themes.association: FAO reports that palm leaves are woven into baskets and that Phragmites and Cyperus papyrus are used for mats in Mozambique, with a growing number of small palm-leaf enterprises in Maputo.

sources.title: Non-wood forest products in Africa: a regional and national overview

themes.label: Aluminium
themes.association: Unwrought aluminium was Mozambique's third-largest export in 2023 at about US$1.09 billion, World Bank WITS data show, behind coal and liquefied natural gas.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Mozambique

countries.name: Namibia
countries.introduction: Namibia's desert coast, cattle country and northern communal lands support diamonds, uranium, beef and fish exports. Swakara pelts, palm-leaf baskets and other non-wood forest products carry craft traditions into markets in southern Africa and beyond.

themes.label: Beef
themes.association: Namibia's Livestock and Livestock Products Board administers the Farm Assured Namibian Meat (FAN Meat) scheme and the NamLITS traceability system, and manages a Norway beef quota.

sources.title: Livestock and Livestock Products Board of Namibia

themes.label: Diamonds
themes.association: Namdeb, owned in equal shares by the Namibian government and De Beers, mines diamonds along the southwest coast around Oranjemund and at satellite operations near Lüderitz and the Orange River.

themes.label: Fish
themes.association: Frozen fish fillets were Namibia's fourth-largest export in 2023 at about US$355 million, per World Bank WITS, and the Namibia Fish Consumption Promotion Trust works to improve domestic access to fish.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Namibia

themes.label: Uranium
themes.association: Uranium ores and concentrates were Namibia's second-largest export in 2023 at about US$778 million, according to World Bank WITS.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Namibia

themes.label: Swakara pelts
themes.association: Agra states that Swakara pelts come from Namibia's arid regions, that it managed the Swakara Board and sorted and marketed all pelts until 31 March 2022, and that the Swakara Breeders' Society dates from 1919.

themes.label: Basketry
themes.association: FAO's regional review values Namibian basketry at N$16.4 million within N$65.3 million of non-wood forest product value, including Hyphaene palm-leaf baskets and mopane-based Mahangu basketry.

sources.title: Non-wood forest products in Africa: a regional and national overview

countries.name: South Africa
countries.introduction: South Africa spans winter-rainfall vineyards, summer-grain plateaus and subtropical cane fields in KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga. Wine, citrus, rooibos, mohair, grain and sugar are established export industries with organised producer bodies and nationally recognised industry standards.

themes.label: Rooibos
themes.association: The South African Rooibos Council states that rooibos is native to the Cederberg, that it was the first African food granted EU Protected Designation of Origin, and that about 20,000 tonnes are produced a year, half consumed locally.

themes.label: Wine
themes.association: Wines of South Africa is the industry's export promotion body, and Vinpro represents close to 2,600 South African wine producers, cellars and industry stakeholders.

themes.label: Citrus
themes.association: The Citrus Growers Association of Southern Africa represents growers in regions including Limpopo, Mpumalanga and the Western Cape and works on market access and quality assurance.

sources.title: Citrus Growers Association of Southern Africa

themes.label: Mohair
themes.association: Mohair South Africa promotes the fibre through the Responsible Mohair Standard and Oritain traceability, connecting Angora goat farmers to brokers, processors, spinners, dye houses and manufacturers.

themes.label: Grain and maize
themes.association: Grain SA represents over 7,852 commercial and 5,891 emerging grain producers growing maize, wheat, sunflower, soybeans, barley, canola, groundnuts and sorghum.

themes.label: Sugar
themes.association: The South African Sugar Association describes a R24 billion industry in Mpumalanga and KwaZulu-Natal that ranks in the global top 25 of about 120 sugar-producing countries.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.introduction: Zambia's copperbelt drives export earnings, while maize, soya, cotton and sugar cane support farm livelihoods across the plateau. Honey and basketry from forest-based enterprises add smaller but widespread rural income, particularly among beekeepers in the north-western provinces.

themes.label: Copper
themes.association: The Zambia Development Agency describes Zambia as the world's seventh-largest copper producer with 6% of reserves, and World Bank WITS shows unrefined copper and copper cathodes as the country's two largest exports in 2023.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Zambia

themes.label: Sugar
themes.association: Zambia Sugar describes itself as Africa's largest single-mill cane sugar producer, operating the Nakambala estate in Mazabuka and selling under the Whitespoon brand into SADC and COMESA markets.

themes.label: Cotton
themes.association: The Cotton Board of Zambia, established under the Cotton Act No. 21 of 2005, regulates seed cotton production and ginning and registers buyers and ginners.

themes.label: Soybeans
themes.association: FAO's Zambia office reports that the soybean value chain has expanded rapidly to become the country's second most important crop after maize.

themes.label: Honey
themes.association: FAO's regional review calls honey and beeswax among Zambia's most important non-wood forest products, estimating national output above 1,500 tonnes a year and some 6,000 beekeepers with 500,000 hives in the north-west.

sources.title: Non-wood forest products in Africa: a regional and national overview

themes.label: Basketry
themes.association: FAO reports that basketry is the most important activity in Zambia's small-scale forest industry, with 60.3% of forest-based enterprises making baskets, mats or hats, largely from bamboo.

sources.title: Non-wood forest products in Africa: a regional and national overview

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.introduction: Zimbabwe's highveld farms, eastern tea estates and mineral belts shape its export economy. Tobacco and gold lead recorded trade, with tea, macadamia, horticulture, leather goods and stone sculpture among the sectors the national trade promotion body promotes for export.

themes.label: Tobacco
themes.association: Tobacco, partly or wholly stemmed, was Zimbabwe's second-largest export in 2023 at about US$1.17 billion, World Bank WITS data show, behind semi-manufactured gold.

sources.title: World Bank WITS — Country Profile: Zimbabwe

themes.label: Tea
themes.association: Tanganda Tea Company operates five estates in Chipinge cropped with tea, coffee, avocados and macadamia, and runs a tea blending and packaging plant in Mutare.

themes.label: Stone sculpture and crafts
themes.association: ZimTrade promotes an arts and crafts export sector and describes Zimbabwean crafts as ranging from intricate stone sculptures to beadwork and woven baskets.

themes.label: Leather goods
themes.association: ZimTrade lists leather products among Zimbabwe's export sectors and describes the country's leather goods as authentic.

themes.label: Horticulture
themes.association: ZimTrade identifies horticulture as an export sector and refers to a diverse range of Zimbabwean horticultural crops.

themes.label: Macadamia
themes.association: Tanganda's Chipinge estates are cropped with macadamia nuts alongside tea, coffee and avocados, according to the company.
